question: Your extraction system reads shipping manifests and fills a JSON schema for each one. On the synchronous Claude API, Claude calls a lookup_port_code tool, your code returns the code, and Claude then completes the record. After the team moved the nightly run to the Message Batches API, most responses ended with stop_reason "tool_use" and no completed record. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The Message Batches API cannot run the port lookup mid-request and send its result back to Claude within the same request.
options.reason: The guide states that the Message Batches API does not support multi-turn tool calling, so each request stops at the tool call without a finished record.

options.text: The 24-hour processing window of the Message Batches API ran out before the port codes arrived, so each extraction was cut off before Claude could finish it.
options.reason: The 24-hour window is only the maximum processing time, and the responses did come back; the real cause is that the Message Batches API never returns tool results to Claude mid-request.

options.text: Duplicate custom_id values made the Message Batches API match each response to the wrong manifest request in the results.
options.reason: The guide describes custom_id as the field that correlates requests with responses; a correlation error would mismatch records, but it would not make responses stop at a tool call.

options.text: The 50% cost savings of the Message Batches API come from a smaller model that cannot produce the complete JSON schema output.
options.reason: The guide names the 50% cost savings but no smaller model; the responses stopped because the Message Batches API has no multi-turn tool calling.
